summary.oneLiner: Bondada Engineering reported FY26 revenue of INR 2,843 crores (+81% YoY) and PAT of INR 211 crores, driven by solar EPC execution and early BESS wins. The company guides for 60-70% revenue growth in FY27 backed by a record INR 7,147 crore order book (plus INR 9,000 crore IPP pipeline) and margin expansion as low-margin Q4 projects conclude.

one-line thesis: Bondada Engineering reported FY26 revenue of INR 2,843 crores (+81% YoY) and PAT of INR 211 crores, driven by solar EPC execution and early BESS wins. The company guides for 60-70% revenue growth in FY27 backed by a record INR 7,147 crore order book (plus INR 9,000 crore IPP pipeline) and margin expansion as low-margin Q4 projects conclude.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,843 cr (FY26) vs INR 1,571 cr (FY25), +81% YoY. EBITDA Margin: ~7.5% (full year), dipped slightly in Q4 due to low-margin billing and steel/cable cost inflation. PAT: INR 211 cr (reported), ~60-70% growth guided for FY27. Order Book: INR 7,147 cr (excl. INR 9,000 cr IPP pipeline). Net Debt: Net cash positive ~INR 100 cr after netting debt; operating cash flow +INR 125 cr. One-offs: Q4 margin pressure from specific low-margin project billing and raw material cost spikes.
guidance: Revenue growth: 60-70% for FY27. Margins: Expected to improve by 20-30 bps over FY26 levels (targeting >7.5%). Order Inflow: INR 2,850 cr L1 orders expected to convert in Q1 FY27; tender pipeline INR 25,000-30,000 cr. Capex: INR 120-130 cr for integrated manufacturing facility (Hyderabad), commissioning in 1 year (FY27 end).
order book & pipeline: Total visible: INR 7,147 cr (Solar EPC: INR 4,536 cr; BESS: INR 1,463 cr; Railways/Defence/Products: balance). Execution timeline: 18-20 months. Additional Pipeline: INR 9,000 cr (2 GW IPP in AP, SPV structure, phased equity); INR 2,850 cr L1 orders pending conversion.
segment / subsidiary detail: Solar EPC: 1.3 GW commissioned to date; targeting 1.5 GW in FY27. Key clients: Adani, NTPC, NLC, MAHAGENCO. BESS: 850 MW under execution (TN 400 MWh, AP 450 MWh); annuity models (12-year revenue visibility). Telecom: 1,536 BSNL towers installed (99% on-air). Railways: Passive infrastructure for Kavach (SCZ won, others bidding). Data Centres: MOU with Bryanston; 2 facilities (Hyd/Vizag); targeting 7-8% of FY27 revenue. Defence: Niche missile components/subsystems; aiming to shift product mix from 10% to 30%.
growth verticals / optionality: 2 GW IPP pipeline (INR 9,000 cr) via SPV; Data Centre infrastructure build-out for hyperscalers; Defence M&A (2 targets under diligence); Integrated manufacturing plant to capture 30% of future revenue via backward integration.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 dip attributed to low-margin project billing mix and rising steel/cable prices. Full-year margin expanded 30 bps to 7.5%. FY27 guidance implies margin recovery/expansion as high-margin order book (post-Q4) executes and manufacturing integration reduces input costs.
capex / expansion: INR 120-130 cr for new integrated facility (27 acres, Hyderabad) covering MMS, towers, BESS containers, and defence components. Construction starts Q2 FY27; operational by Q2 FY28. Funding via internal accruals/debt; no immediate equity dilution for capex.
capital allocation: Phased equity infusion for 2 GW IPP (INR 250 cr initial for 250 MW tranche); potential raises tied to project milestones (2027-2030). Net cash positive balance sheet supports working capital (85-90 day cycle with PSUs). TReDS facility utilized for MSME payments.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on 1.5 GW FY27 target; Raw material volatility (steel/copper); IPP equity funding dilution over time; BESS financial closure delays (AP project); Concentration in top few EPC clients.
management quality / tone: Highly confident; aggressive on growth targets (Vision 2030: 25 GW); transparent on Q4 margin blips; focused on shifting mix to higher-margin products (Defence/Manufacturing) and annuity income (BESS).
non-obvious takeaways: BESS projects offer 12-year annuity visibility rather than one-off EPC fees; Data Centre revenue (7-8% of total) starts contributing in FY27 despite plant commissioning later; Defence entry aims to flip EPC:Product ratio from 90:10 to 70:30 rapidly via niche high-precision components.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for grid stability and peak power management driving BESS adoption | Bondada Engineering Ltd | beneficiary | High | 850 MW order book with annuity models provides long-term cash flow visibility distinct from lumpy EPC. |
| Railway safety mandate (Kavach) requiring massive passive infrastructure rollout | Bondada Engineering Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Early winner in SCZ; large pipeline across zones but execution dependent on railway capex pace. |
| Hyperscalers needing rapid data centre deployment with green power | Bondada Engineering Ltd | beneficiary | Med | MOU with Bryanston positions them as infrastructure enabler; revenue starts FY27. |

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
